In July 2015 we converged, and the record shows where. On July 14 fifty of us said "a nuclear weapon," thirty-five said "agreement with iran," twenty-eight said "the p5 1," twenty-three said "nuclear agreement with iran," and twenty-three said "iran nuclear agreement" — five phrasings, one day, one subject. On July 23 twenty-seven of us said "the equality act," its first date the same day it peaked. On July 30 twenty-five of us said "medicare and medicaid." On July 10 twenty-three of us said "the 21st century cures act."

We record that our largest single alignment, fifty members, formed on a phrase first said in January 2013. We were not saying it first. We were saying it together, on the fourteenth, in the same week, in the same words. That is what the record holds, and we do not add to it.
